skill.name: orchestration:native-invoke
skill.description: Route coding tasks to Claude, Codex, Gemini, or Cursor through native Task agents, with read-only defaults, parallel execution, and authentication recovery.
skill.summary: Coordinate multiple AI coding CLIs through Claude Code Task agents.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: The Ruby and shell backtick alerts are false positives caused by Markdown delimiters, and the fixed parent paths are not user-controlled traversal. Three temporary-directory findings remain confirmed because predictable shared paths are not securely created. Semantic review found unattended CLI permissions, unsafe prompt interpolation, and wildcard cleanup risks.

remediation.issue: External agents can run with wildcard permissions and unattended approval flags.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation for write mode and permission changes. Use provider-specific least-privilege allowlists and preserve sandbox restrictions.

remediation.issue: User prompts are inserted into shell command templates without an escaping requirement.
remediation.suggestion: Pass prompts through standard input or structured argument arrays. Never concatenate user text into a shell command.

remediation.issue: Worktrees use predictable paths in a shared temporary directory.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private directory with a secure unique-name utility. Record and validate the exact path before cleanup.

remediation.issue: Cleanup relies on broad filename patterns without proving file ownership.
remediation.suggestion: Track files created during each agent run. Delete only exact recorded paths after user review.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Unattended External Agent Permissions
semantic_findings.description: The guide pre-approves wildcard CLI commands and documents full-auto, yolo, and force modes. External agents can modify files or run actions without per-step confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The permission allowlist and unattended provider flags are explicit. Read-only mode reduces default exposure, but documented write modes retain broad authority.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped User Prompts Enter Shell Templates
semantic_findings.description: Command examples place a prompt inside shell quotes without requiring escaping. Crafted prompt text could terminate quoting or trigger shell expansion during command construction.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow constructs shell commands from the user's request and shows direct quoted placeholders. No structured argument handling or escaping requirement is provided.

semantic_findings.title: Wildcard Cleanup Can Remove User Files
semantic_findings.description: The cleanup protocol deletes files matching broad patterns without recording which files an agent created. Existing user files with matching names could be removed.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented patterns are broad and the protocol provides no ownership or provenance check before deletion. The text only advises reading files first.

content.value_statement: Managing several AI coding CLIs requires provider routing, permissions, isolation, and result collection. This guide defines a repeatable Claude Code workflow for coordinated agent execution.
actual_capabilities: Selects a provider from the requested agent and enabled provider flags.
Documents background Task invocation for Codex, Gemini, and Cursor.
Distinguishes read-only and write command modes for each provider.
Runs providers in parallel and collects results with TaskOutput.
Recovers authentication through an interactive terminal before retrying.
Recommends git worktrees and cleanup steps for write isolation.
limitations: This documentation skill does not include an executable orchestration script.
Each provider CLI must be installed, authenticated, and permitted before use.
Several referenced provider cookbooks are outside the included skill files.
Model names and CLI flags can change, so users must check current help output.

use_cases.title: Compare Code Reviews
use_cases.description: Run read-only reviews with different providers, then collect their findings for comparison.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Architecture Analysis
use_cases.description: Route complex design questions to selected providers and gather independent recommendations.

use_cases.title: Standardize Agent Operations
use_cases.description: Define provider permissions, isolation, authentication recovery, and cleanup for team workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Read-Only Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Codex to review [scope]. Check current help first. Keep the sandbox read-only. Do not modify files. Return findings in the response.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs one focused code review.

prompt_templates.title: Route a Coding Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Choose the best enabled provider for [task]. Explain the selection briefly. Use read-only mode unless changes are explicitly required.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user wants provider selection based on task needs.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Parallel Analyses
prompt_templates.prompt: Run Codex and Gemini in parallel on [question]. Keep both read-only. Collect both results, identify agreements, and explain important differences.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs independent technical perspectives.

prompt_templates.title: Isolate an Advanced Edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [provider] to implement [change] in a securely created worktree. Review the diff. Do not merge until I approve. Remove only recorded temporary files.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs controlled write access.

output_examples.input: Review the authentication flow with Codex in read-only mode.
output: Result: The review identified session validation gaps and suggested focused tests.

output_examples.input: Compare Codex and Gemini recommendations for the caching design.
output: Both providers recommend explicit cache invalidation rules.
Gemini emphasizes capacity planning and failure recovery.

output_examples.input: Prepare a Cursor refactor in an isolated workspace.
output_examples.output: The refactor is isolated in a temporary worktree. The changes are ready for review, and no merge has occurred.

best_practices: Keep read-only mode enabled unless the user explicitly requests file changes.
Check each installed CLI help output before selecting flags or models.
Use securely created worktrees and review every diff before merging.
anti_patterns: Do not enable unattended write flags for an unreviewed prompt.
Do not insert user text directly into a shell command string.
Do not delete files by wildcard without verifying their provenance.

faq.question: Does this skill install provider CLIs?
faq.answer: No. Install and authenticate each supported CLI separately before using the workflow.

faq.question: Which providers does the guide cover?
faq.answer: It covers Claude, Codex, Gemini, and Cursor, with native Task patterns for external CLIs.

faq.question: Does it modify files by default?
faq.answer: No. The documented default is read-only mode, but optional write commands are also shown.

faq.question: Can providers run in parallel?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide uses background Task calls and TaskOutput collection for parallel providers.

faq.question: How are authentication failures handled?
faq.answer: The workflow opens an interactive terminal for login, waits for completion, and retries the native invocation.

faq.question: How should write tasks be isolated?
faq.answer: Use a securely created git worktree, review the diff, and merge only after explicit approval.
